contextual.summary: King's makes contextual offers of up to two A-level grades below the advertised offer to UK-based applicants who completed K+, received free school meals, or are care-experienced/care leavers or estranged.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two A-level grades lower than the advertised entry requirements (AAB instead of A*AA on the courses recorded here)

criteria.detail: Successfully completed King's Social Mobility and Widening Participation programme K+
Have been in receipt of free school meals (FSM)

contextual.rulesText: Applicants must meet at least one of the criteria ('And/Or') to be considered for a contextual offer; contextual admissions are only for UK-based applicants and an offer is not guaranteed. A separate 'additional consideration' route (not a reduced offer) covers applicants who completed a qualifying King's widening participation programme, attended King's College London Maths School, took a qualifying IntoUniversity course, or have forced displacement or are young adult carers. The page states it applies to September 2026 entry.

source.evidence: Applicants must meet at least one of the criteria outlined below to be considered for a contextual offer: Have successfully completed King's College London's Social Mobility and Widening Participation programme K+

programmes.name: K+
programmes.summary: King's flagship two-year widening participation programme for sixth-form students, with pathways by subject area (including Business, and Social Science & Public Policy covering Economics, PPE, Political Economy and Politics).
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students at non-selective state schools or colleges in Greater London or one of King's target regions, with 8 GCSEs at grades 4-9 (including English and Maths, at least five at 6-9) and no parent/carer who has completed university.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Currently in Year 12; live or attend a school in Greater London or one of King's target regions; attend a non-selective state school; 8 GCSEs at grades 4-9 (including English and Maths) with at least five at grades 6-9; no parent/carer who has completed university (still considered if a parent/carer is studying their first degree, graduated in the last ten years or completed a degree in another country). Some pathways have extra subject and grade requirements. Grade requirements may be waived for care-experienced, estranged, forced migrant, Gypsy/Roma/Traveller and homeless or sofa-surfing students.
benefits: Two-grade reduced offer for most courses at King's after successfully completing K+
£1,000 bursary in the first year if you come to King's
Academic taster sessions, study skills, UCAS and student finance guidance, and a spring or summer school
King's can cover travel costs to K+ events for participants living outside London
programmes.offerReduction: Two-grade reduced offer for most courses (the K+ variable offer is worth up to two A-level grades lower than the standard offer)
programmes.subjects: Pathways by subject area, e.g. Business (Accounting, Business, Finance or Management) and Social Science & Public Policy (Economics, PPE, Political Economy, Politics)

runs.text: 2026 dates (2025-27 cohort): Business spring school 7-11 April 2026; Social Science & Public Policy summer school 10-14 August 2026 (summer induction 18 July 2026). 2027 dates not announced.

opens.text: Spring pathways (including Business) reopen in late 2026; summer pathways (including Social Science & Public Policy) reopen in 2027. No exact dates given.

programmes.infoNote: Based on the 2025-27 cohort's published dates. The page says to complete an expression-of-interest form if you are in Year 12 (as of September 2026) to be told when applications open. It also says 'Applications for our Summer Pathways will open on 5 May' without giving a year.

source.evidence: Students who successfully complete K+ also get a two-grade reduced offer for most courses at King's College London and a £1000 bursary in the first year if they decide to come to us.

notConfirmed: cost: the page doesn't say whether K+ is free

programmes.name: Pre-University Summer School
programmes.summary: One-week subject courses in central London for 16-17 year olds (with an optional residential package), including Business Management, Accounting and Finance, Politics and International Relations.
programmes.whoCanApply: Academically motivated students aged 16 or 17 who are about to start or are in their final three years of high school (you must turn 16 before the start date and not turn 18 until after the programme ends).
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open to students aged 16-17 (not 18 before the programme ends); applicants must be independent, mature and motivated. No widening participation criteria; a paid programme.
